correctness.rationale: Every derivation preserves the one-dimensional derived center, so its unique parameters (a,T,f) obey exactly the bilinear conformal-symplectic equation. The equation D²=D forces a in {0,1}, an idempotent T, and a linear condition on f. Comparing the 0 and 1 eigenspaces of T in the bilinear equation proves the complementary-Lagrangian case for a=1, the trivial a=0 case for odd characteristic, and the nondegenerate orthogonal splitting case for characteristic two. The finite-field formula follows from established symplectic-group stabilizers and exact f-vector-space cardinalities. Each reduced geometric stratum is a vector bundle on an explicitly specified open Grassmannian or transverse-Lagrangian-pair base; distinct characteristic polynomials separate strata. The standalone checker directly tested original Leibniz and square-one equations in complete small-field cases, including the true four-element extension field. An infinite proof is in RESULT.md; finite testing is corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The historical classification of Heisenberg group gradings up to equivalence (Calderón et al., arXiv:1405.4093, Theorem 1) substantially precedes the homogeneous symplectic-basis structural normal form; that is acknowledged and not claimed new. The narrower assessed finding is the explicit count of labeled idempotent ordinary derivations at each possible rank, for every finite field, coupled to dimensions and smooth component counts of the reduced solution variety. The most relevant complete available primary text treats gradings and their automorphism symmetries but does not give these quantitative invariants. Eick–Moede (arXiv:2205.03155) treat inner idempotents ad(l) and finite-field simple Lie algebras; the nonzero idempotent derivations here are outer on nilpotent Heisenberg algebras. Closely related indexed records treat subalgebra statistics, square-zero derivations, and local derivations, not projector-derivation rank distributions. An unidentified broader grading-counting theorem remains a priority risk; no assertion of independent certification is made.

value.rationale: The exact rank distribution of all labeled projector-derivations is a natural operator invariant for each Heisenberg Lie algebra over every finite field; it is not the number of equivalence classes of Z/2-gradings. The formula combines symplectic nondegenerate-summand geometry and Lagrangian incidence in a sharp characteristic dichotomy, gives every nonempty rank with its multiplicity, and determines component number, smoothness and dimensions of an infinite family of reduced parameter varieties. The effect is structural and arithmetic, not an arbitrary low-dimensional table or a normalization check. No result for general nilpotent Lie algebras or unreduced schemes is claimed.
